chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the ritual bath (ghusl) when pelting the Jamarah. So he said: 'Sometimes I do so, and as for it being from the Sunnah, then no (it is not), but it is due to the heat and the sweat.'
ai.seo_question: Is the ghusl after pelting the Jamarah a mandatory Sunnah or a recommended act due to physical necessity?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between a ritual bath driven by religious obligation and one motivated by physical necessity, noting that while he personally performs ghusl after pelting the Jamarah, it is primarily due to the intense heat and sweat rather than being a strict Sunnah. This reflects the Shia juristic principle of distinguishing between *Sunnah Mu'akkadah* (emphasized tradition) and *Mustahabb* (recommended) acts based on practical context. The narration highlights the flexibility in Shia fiqh, where personal practice by the Imam can serve as a model without necessarily establishing a binding legal requirement for all followers.
